citation: Walther B, Karl JP, Booth SL, Boyaval P. Menaquinones, bacteria, and the food supply: the relevance of dairy and fermented food products. Adv Nutr. 2013;4(4):463-73, Table 2
table: Table 2, representative ranges of measured menaquinone concentration in dairy foods and fermented food products
quotes: Schurgers LJ, Vermeer C. Determination of phylloquinone and menaquinones in food. Haemostasis. 2000;30:298-307 (reference 28)
Kamao M, Suhara Y, Tsugawa N, et al. Vitamin K content of foods and dietary vitamin K intake in Japanese young women. J Nutr Sci Vitaminol. 2007;53:464-70 (reference 29)
note: A review reporting the two primary studies rather than a study in its own right, which is why both are named above. ND is not detectable. Only the two plant rows are transcribed here; the dairy, cheese and salami rows of the same table are foods this page does not carry. The table has no column for a menaquinone total and none is recorded here, because summing across homologues would be this repository's arithmetic and not the source's.
finding: The sauerkraut row sums to 4.8 ug across its six reported homologues, which is the figure this page previously carried as sauerkraut MK-7. MK-7 in sauerkraut is 0.2 ug; 4.8 is the total.
mk11: The review does not report MK-11 for any food and its table has no column for it.
